sections.title: What is Topological Sort?
sections.content:
Topological sort takes a **Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)** and produces a linear ordering of its nodes such that for every directed edge u→v, node u appears before v. Dependencies must come first.

Real-world examples: course prerequisites, npm package install order, Makefile compilation order. All are topological sort on a dependency DAG.

Critical constraint: **topological sort only exists for DAGs**. A cycle means no valid linear ordering exists — A depends on B, B depends on A, neither can go first. This is why topological sort algorithms double as cycle detectors: if the output doesn't contain all nodes, a cycle exists.

Two standard implementations: **Kahn's algorithm** (BFS-based, repeatedly remove in-degree-0 nodes — intuitive and easy to explain) and **DFS post-order** (push nodes after all descendants are processed). Both O(V+E). Kahn's is generally preferred in interviews.

sections.title: When to Use This
sections.content: Use topological sort when a problem involves ordering items with dependencies. Keywords: 'course prerequisites', 'build order', 'find a valid ordering', 'task dependencies'. Also for cycle detection in directed graphs — if sort can't include all nodes, a cycle exists.

sections.title: Kahn's Algorithm and DFS-Based Sort
sections.content:
## Kahn's Algorithm (BFS-Based)

1. Compute `inDegree[v]` for all nodes.
2. Enqueue all nodes with `inDegree = 0`.
3. While queue not empty: dequeue node, add to result, decrement `inDegree[neighbor]` for each neighbor. If `inDegree[neighbor]` reaches 0, enqueue it.
4. If `result.length < n`, a cycle exists.

## DFS-Based Topological Sort

Run DFS. When a node is **fully processed** (all descendants done), push to stack. Read stack top-to-bottom for topological order. Post-order reversal gives dependency-first ordering.

## Edge Direction

'Course A is prerequisite for B' → edge A→B. Build `graph[A].push(B)` and `inDegree[B]++`. Reversed edges give a backwards topological order.

## Cycle Detection Summary

Kahn's: `result.length < n` → cycle. DFS: encountering a gray node → cycle. Both detect the same condition; Kahn's detection is more explicit.

## Multiple Valid Orderings

Topological sort is not unique. For lexicographically smallest, use a min-heap instead of a queue in Kahn's.

sections.title: Core Template
sections.explanation: Kahn's algorithm with in-degree array and BFS queue. Cycle detection is built-in: incomplete result means some nodes had in-degree that never reached 0.

items.name: DFS-Based Topological Sort
items.description: Post-order DFS pushes each node to a stack after all descendants are processed. Reverse the stack for topological order. Useful when already doing DFS for cycle detection with color states.

items.name: Lexicographic Topological Sort
items.description: Replace the queue in Kahn's with a min-heap. When multiple nodes have in-degree 0, always process the smallest first. Produces the lexicographically smallest valid ordering.

items.name: Find Safe Nodes (Reverse Topological)
items.description: Reverse all edges and run Kahn's. Nodes appearing in the topological order of the reversed graph are safe (don't lead to cycles) in the original graph.

sections.title: Complexity
sections.explanation: Kahn's processes each node once on dequeue (O(V)) and each edge once when decrementing in-degrees (O(E)). Space is O(V+E) for the adjacency list, O(V) for in-degree array and queue.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Building edges in the wrong direction — 'A is prerequisite for B' means A→B. Reversed edges produce a backwards topological order.
Not checking result.length === numNodes after Kahn's — a cycle silently produces an incomplete result. Always check.
Applying topological sort to undirected graphs — undefined for undirected edges which don't encode ordering.
Assuming topological sort gives a unique result — multiple valid orderings exist; don't test for a specific one unless the problem asks for lexicographically smallest.
In alien dictionary: comparing 'abc' and 'ab' where the shorter word comes after the longer prefix is an invalid dictionary (implies a cycle), not derivable ordering.

items.title: Find Eventual Safe States
items.why: Reverse graph + Kahn's variant — safe nodes appear in topological order after reversing edges.

sections.title: What to Learn Next
sections.why: Shortest paths extend BFS to weighted graphs. Dijkstra combines the priority queue from heaps with BFS-style expansion. Topological sort also enables O(V+E) shortest/longest path in DAGs.
